title: Parametrized test loop (Python)
description: One test body over a table of (input, expected) pairs beats copy-pasted test functions. Failures name the case that broke. Worked example: run 4 square cases mentally — inputs bind as written, each step follows the code path described below, and the final value is 4 passed.
how_it_works: The loop runs the same assertion per case; the assert message identifies the failing input.

test_cases.note: Determinism check: re-running the snippet reproduces the identical output.

pitfalls: One bad case aborts the rest — frameworks run all and report each.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Parametrized test loop (Python)
demo.program:
# JAH demo program — jahdb-demo-1.0
# Database: code-database · Record: JAH-CODE-0000019
# RUN: PC: save as demo.py, run `python3 demo.py`.

def sq(n):
    return n * n

cases = [(0, 0), (2, 4), (-3, 9), (10, 100)]
for n, want in cases:
    assert sq(n) == want, n
print("%d passed" % len(cases))
